page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between single-threaded and multi-threaded execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench tests, with single-threaded gzip compression falling into the bottom 10%. However, the 32 dedicated vCPUs deliver average multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all scoring in the middle 50%. Memory read bandwidth reaches 92.61 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though the overall PassMark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance utilizes an older generation Intel Xeon architecture, which offers a lower-cost entry point for high-vCPU workloads compared to newer silicon generations, albeit with lower per-core efficiency. It is appropriate for multi-threaded workloads that can parallelize across 32 cores without requiring high single-thread performance or local SSD storage. Suitable workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded compilation, Redis caching, and medium-scale database operations.
